first_impression.reaction: I googled this because James's sister did a sand thing at her wedding and I wasn't sure if it's lovely or a bit naff. The intro is calm and tells me exactly what I'm getting: words the celebrant can read, a template, what to put on the table, and beach questions. No 'dream day' rubbish. I kept going.

journey.quote: A sand ceremony asks very little of you on the day, which is exactly why the words around it matter.
journey.reaction: Good opening. Understated, and it gets why we'd care about the wording.

journey.quote: The pour sits well after the vows and rings and before the pronouncement, and your celebrant sets the final order.
journey.reaction: 'Well after'? Later the article says 'just before the celebrant pronounces them married'. Which is it? Small thing, but it made me stop and reread.

journey.section: Sand ceremony script, word for word
journey.quote: Take your time. There is no right way to do this, only yours.
journey.reaction: Nice. Takes the pressure off. I can picture a celebrant saying that without it sounding rehearsed.

journey.quote: Two colours, one vessel, and no way to tell where one of you ends and the other begins.
journey.reaction: Edging towards sappy, and the whole point of the glass is you can see the layers. I'd probably use the short version or the secular one instead. Not a deal-breaker.

journey.quote: This ceremony is about two people choosing each other, willingly and on purpose.
journey.reaction: This is us. Grown-up, not gushing. I'd screenshot this one for James.

journey.section: Sample wording: with parents or both families
journey.quote: Their parents, [Names] and [Names], have been invited to begin this pour, one colour from each family.
journey.reaction: Our parents are paying for a big chunk of this, so including them is a genuinely good idea. This is the one I'd send to Mum.

journey.quote: Keep each blank to a sentence. The pour is the moment, not the speech.
journey.reaction: Love this. Honest advice that stops it getting cringe in front of our friends.

journey.quote: brings the venue, travel and vendors together in one plan, anywhere in the world.
journey.reaction: Bit of a sales line dropped into the middle of a template. 'Anywhere in the world' is what every planner says. It doesn't tell me what you actually do.

journey.section: What you need for a sand ceremony
journey.quote: The funnel stays out of sight in case a pour goes wide.
journey.reaction: That's an insider detail. Someone has seen a pour go wrong. More of this, please.

journey.quote: Some couples set it on the guestbook table for the evening, then carry it home wrapped in hand luggage.
journey.reaction: Practical, but it raised a question: if it's beach sand from overseas, can we actually bring it back into Australia? Nobody tells you that.

journey.section: A sand ceremony at a beach or destination wedding
journey.quote: Can the table sit with its back to the wind?
journey.reaction: This whole list is exactly what I'd never think to ask. Wind, who seals it, whether you can take sand. Feels like someone who has done beach ceremonies.

journey.section: A sand ceremony at a beach or destination wedding
journey.quote: Through Wedded Concierge, your Wedded Advisor plans the venue, travel and vendors with you as a single point of contact, working in your time zone.
journey.reaction: One person, our time zone. That's the 'no spreadsheets for 18 months' thing we want. It still doesn't say who's actually standing on the beach on the day if the wind picks up, though.

journey.section: A sand ceremony and the legal words
journey.quote: Either way, ask your celebrant which legal lines they will say, and build the pour around them.
journey.reaction: Quoting the actual Act with links is reassuring, and as a lawyer I appreciate it. The takeaway line is clear and makes the point: sand is decoration, the words are what count.

journey.quote: The pour sits well after the vows and rings, just before the pronouncement, or straight after the welcome.
journey.reaction: Same 'well after' wording again, and here it sits right next to 'just before the pronouncement'. Reads as contradictory.

journey.section: Planning the ceremony around the pour
journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor is your one point of contact from start to finish, and confirms inclusions in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: 'Confirms inclusions in writing before you commit' is the line that speaks to my hidden-costs fear. Soft close, no hard sell. Good.

unanswered_questions: If we use sand from an overseas beach, are we allowed to bring it back into Australia in hand luggage?
Who is actually on the ground on the day (setting the table, sealing the vessel, dealing with wind) if our Wedded Advisor is working in our time zone?
Does Wedded Concierge sort the vessel, sand and table, or do we bring our own?
Is there a real wedding with venue and date where a couple did a sand ceremony, so we can see how it looks in photos?
If we marry symbolically abroad, how does the legal part in Australia fit around the trip?

turn_offs_found.quote: brings the venue, travel and vendors together in one plan, anywhere in the world.
turn_offs_found.why: 'Anywhere in the world' is generic planner-speak, and putting a pitch in the middle of the template feels a little salesy.

cta_reaction.quote: Your Wedded Advisor is your one point of contact from start to finish, and confirms inclusions in writing before you commit. Start the conversation with Wedded Concierge.
cta_reaction.why: It's calm and the 'in writing' bit lands. But I came for a script, we haven't chosen a destination, and I'd want to see a real wedding before I talk to anyone. I'd bookmark the site and read a couple more posts.

top_3_changes: Fix the contradictory placement wording in two places. Key takeaways: old "The pour sits well after the vows and rings and before the pronouncement, and your celebrant sets the final order." new "The pour usually sits after the vows and rings and just before the pronouncement, and your celebrant sets the final order." FAQ: old "The pour sits well after the vows and rings, just before the pronouncement, or straight after the welcome." new "The pour sits after the vows and rings, just before the pronouncement, or straight after the welcome."

Drop the generic claim from the mid-article CTA. Old "brings the venue, travel and vendors together in one plan, anywhere in the world." new "brings the venue, travel and vendors together in one plan."

Tone down the sappy closing line, which also contradicts the visible layers. Old "Two colours, one vessel, and no way to tell where one of you ends and the other begins." new "Two colours, one vessel, and every layer still there to see."

checks.check: Every journey point, turn-off and CTA reaction has an exact quote from the draft
Stayed in character as Sophie & James (Sydney, early research, no destination chosen)
No invented brand facts; unknowns placed in unanswered_questions
HTML comments, image slots and fact markers treated as invisible
Suggested edits are exact old/new strings, add no new facts, and stay clear of fees, commissions, supplier and celebrant sourcing or vetting

open_questions.question: The 'carry it home in hand luggage' line prompts an obvious question about bringing overseas beach sand into Australia. The draft makes no claim about it. Should a sourced line or [[VERIFY]] be considered by the writer, or is it out of scope for this post?
Is there a real wedding with a sand ceremony (venue and date) the post could link to? This persona usually needs one before enquiring.

assumptions: Persona card is provisional (not CRM-calibrated); reactions reflect the assumed profile.
Assumed the couple are weighing a sand ceremony after seeing one at a family wedding, which explains a script search at the early research stage.
Draft read in rendered form, so HTML comment image slots and fact tags were ignored, and link text was read as plain text.
